title: Artificial intelligence across the gastric cancer care continuum: Clinical evidence, multimodal integration, and translation

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Artificial intelligence across the gastric cancer care continuum: Clinical evidence, multimodal integration, and translation》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · p0010】Gastric cancer continues to impose a substantial global burden despite declining age-standardized incidence and mortality rates in some regions.1 According to Global Cancer Observatory (GLOBOCAN) 2022, stomach cancer accounted for more than 968,000 new cases and nearly 660,000 deaths worldwide,2 underscoring its status as one of the deadliest common malignancies.2 The burden remains especially high in East Asia, where organized screening programs and high procedural volumes have made early detection a central clinical priority.3 Nevertheless, many patients are still diagnosed at locally advanced or metastatic stages.4 Early lesions may be endoscopically subtle, symptoms are often nonspecific, and the disease exhibits marked histologic, molecular, and spatial heterogeneities. Gastric cancer is, therefore, not only a high-burden disease but also one that is highly prone to error across the clinical pathway.5

【Introduction · p0015】These clinical challenges align closely with the strengths of modern artificial intelligence (AI).5 Over the past decade, the field has progressed from conventional machine learning models based on limited structured variables to deep neural networks capable of analyzing high-dimensional image data.5 More recently, the field has moved toward multimodal and foundation model paradigms that learn transferable representations from large, weakly labeled, or unlabeled datasets.6 In gastric cancer, this transition is especially consequential because management depends on integrating heterogeneous data streams, including white-light and image-enhanced endoscopy, computed tomography (CT) and positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT), histopathology, immunophenotyping, molecular testing, laboratory findings, and treatment trajectories.7 Few solid tumors illustrate the need for cross-modal clinical AI as clearly as gastric cancer.8

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Artificial intelligence across the gastric cancer care continuum: Clinical evidence, multimodal integration, and translation》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Review design · p0040】This review was not prospectively registered and not designed as a formal systematic review. Accordingly, it does not claim full compliance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses. Transparency was instead strengthened through a reproducible search description, explicit eligibility criteria, structured evidence characterization, and an adapted study-identification framework presented.

【Review design · p0035】This article was designed as a structured narrative review addressing the clinical and translational development of AI in gastric cancer. The narrative approach was selected because the evidence spans heterogeneous clinical tasks, data modalities, model architectures, outcome definitions, and study designs that are not suitable for a single pooled quantitative analysis. The conduct and reporting of the review were informed by the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA).

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Artificial intelligence across the gastric cancer care continuum: Clinical evidence, multimodal integration, and translation》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Validation, regulation, and clinical utility · p0340】Most gastric cancer AI studies remain retrospective, and this is the principal limitation on evidence maturity.5 The 2023 real-time endoscopy CDSS is notable because it included prospective multicenter external testing, whereas many otherwise high-performing systems remain confined to retrospective datasets.26 Similarly, the radiomics meta-analysis for peritoneal metastasis reported an AUC of 0.89 but a substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 88%).14 These examples show that model availability is no longer the main constraint; the priority is the consistent clinical evaluation.

【Validation, regulation, and clinical utility · p0345】Several representative studies show why strong discrimination should not be equated with clinical maturity. The peritoneal-metastasis radiomics meta-analysis reported an AUC of 0.89 but a heterogeneity (I2) of 88%.14 In the real-time endoscopy CDSS, four-class accuracy declined from 89.7% internally to 81.5% in multicenter external testing.32 HER2Net declined from 0.9043 internal accuracy to 0.8922 external accuracy,53 while the ICIsRS model reported retrospective AUCs as high as 1.00 without prospective treatment-allocation evidence.19 In a national cohort of more than 10 million screened adults, logistic regression outperformed more complex machine learning approaches.62 These examples support external validation, calibration, realistic prevalence, and comparison with simpler models and standard practice.

Several representative studies show why strong discrimination should not be equated with clinical maturity. The peritoneal-metastasis radiomics meta-analysis reported an AUC of 0.89 but a heterogeneity (I2) of 88%.14 In the real-time endoscopy CDSS, four-class accuracy declined from 89.7% internally to 81.5% in multicenter external testing.32 HER2Net declined from 0.9043 internal accuracy to 0.8922 external accuracy,53 while the ICIsRS model reported retrospective AUCs as high as 1.00 without prospective treatment-allocation evidence.19 In a national cohort of more than 10 million screened adults, logistic regression outperformed more complex machine learning approaches.62 These examples support external validation, calibration, realistic prevalence, and comparison with simpler models and standard practice.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Artificial intelligence across the gastric cancer care continuum: Clinical evidence, multimodal integration, and translation》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Figure 1 · fig1】Figure 1 AI across the gastric cancer care continuumAI applications span prevention and screening prioritization, endoscopic detection and characterization, imaging-based staging, digital pathology and molecular prescreening, prognostic modeling, treatment allocation, and emerging multimodal decision support. Translational maturity is uneven: a real-time endoscopy CDSS retained external multicenter accuracies of 81.5% for four-class classification and 86.4% for invasion-depth assessment, whereas radiomics for peritoneal metastasis achieved a pooled AUC of 0.89 but substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 88%).AI, artificial intelligence; CDSS, clinical decision support system; CT, computed tomography; H&E, hematoxylin and eosin; PET/CT, positron emission tomography/computed tomography.

【Figure 2 · fig2】Figure 2 Near-term clinical role of digital pathology AI in gastric cancerDigital pathology AI can convert routine H&E slides into non-definitive signals for case triage, biomarker prescreening, biomarker enrichment, and treatment-response enrichment. HER2Net achieved accuracies of 0.9043 internally and 0.8922 in external multicenter testing, while the ICIsRS model reported AUCs of 0.92–1.00 across four testing datasets for first-line PD-1 blockade plus chemotherapy. These systems are best positioned as workflow-compatible prioritization layers rather than replacements for confirmatory testing or expert interpretation.AUC, area under the curve; H&E, hematoxylin and eosin; HER2, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2; ICIsRS, immune checkpoint inhibitors response score; IHC, immunohistochemistry; ISH, in situ hybridization; PD-1, programmed cell death protein 1.

【Figure 3 · fig3】Figure 3 Evolution of prognostic AI in gastric cancerPrognostic modeling is shifting from static, single-modality baseline prediction toward spatially informed and multimodal risk assessment. A cell-graph model achieved a binary survival AUC of 0.960 and a ternary C-index of 0.823; a nationwide structured-data model in more than 10 million screened adults achieved an AUC of 0.708; and a multicohort radiopathomics model achieved 5-year OS AUCs of 0.857–0.917 in validation cohorts. Routine pathology-derived spatial representations currently have the greatest workflow compatibility, whereas single-cell and multi-omics data mainly provide upstream mechanism-linked features.AJCC, American Joint Committee on Cancer; AUC, area under the curve; C-index, concordance index; OS, overall survival.
